===== serctl_cli =====
Persistent SSH control suite: encrypted creds + long-lived daemon + IPC

Usage: serctl_cli [COMMAND]

Commands:
  ui                Open the Winit-based desktop workspace (also the default with no command)
  add               Add or update a profile using its independent passphrase
  list              List saved profiles (host/port only — secrets stay sealed)
  remove            Remove a profile
  admin             Initialize or verify the Windows administrator password
  profile-password  Manage one profile's independent passphrase
  recovery          Manage the vault-wide 2-of-2 offline recovery policy
  audit             Inspect or explicitly recover this profile's authenticated audit ledger
  up                Start the global broker in the foreground; profiles unlock per request
  exec              Run a remote command through the on-demand global broker
  upload            Upload a local file without overwriting an existing remote file
  download          Download a remote file without overwriting an existing local file
  transfer          Observable, cancellable file transfer with remote-confirmed progress
  shell             Open an interactive PTY shell through the on-demand global broker
  tunnel            Run a loopback-only SSH TCP tunnel in the foreground until Ctrl+C
  status            Show daemon status
  down              Stop a running daemon after verifying one profile passphrase
  grant-issue       Issue a policy-bounded OperationGrant for an agent frontend
  agent             Run the agent stdio gateway: JSONL requests on stdin, JSONL relay results on stdout, authenticated by an issued OperationGrant
  help              Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version

===== serctl_cli add =====
Add or update a profile using its independent passphrase.

Creating a profile requires administrator authorization on Windows; updating an existing profile requires only that profile's passphrase.

Usage: serctl_cli add [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments:
  [NAME]


Options:
      --host <HOST>


      --user <USER>


      --port <PORT>
          [default: 22]

      --host-key-sha256 <SHA256:FINGERPRINT>
          Expected SSH host-key fingerprint, in `SHA256:...` form

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== serctl_cli admin =====
Initialize or verify the Windows administrator password

Usage: serctl_cli admin <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status           Show whether administrator authorization has been initialized
  init             Initialize the administrator password. Windows only
  verify           Verify administrator authorization without changing state
  change-password  Replace the administrator password after verifying the current one
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli admin change-password =====
Replace the administrator password after verifying the current one

Usage: serctl_cli admin change-password

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli admin init =====
Initialize the administrator password. Windows only

Usage: serctl_cli admin init --recovery-media <FILE>

Options:
      --recovery-media <FILE>
          New 2-of-2 offline recovery share. The path must not already exist

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli admin status =====
Show whether administrator authorization has been initialized

Usage: serctl_cli admin status

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli admin verify =====
Verify administrator authorization without changing state

Usage: serctl_cli admin verify

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli agent =====
Run the agent stdio gateway: JSONL requests on stdin, JSONL relay results on stdout, authenticated by an issued OperationGrant

Usage: serctl_cli agent [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --grant <FILE>
          Grant file previously written by `grant-issue`

      --grant-handle <HANDLE_OR_FD>
          Read the grant once from an inherited HANDLE/fd, then close it

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli audit =====
Inspect or explicitly recover this profile's authenticated audit ledger

Usage: serctl_cli audit <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status           Verify the ledger and report pending operations without changing it
  resolve-unknown  Append Unknown outcomes for all authenticated pending Intents
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli audit resolve-unknown =====
Append Unknown outcomes for all authenticated pending Intents

Usage: serctl_cli audit resolve-unknown [OPTIONS] --acknowledge-unknown-outcome <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


Options:
      --anchor <FILE>
          Optional previously exported checkpoint used as a rollback anchor

      --anchor-output <NEW_FILE>
          Write the post-recovery authenticated checkpoint to a new file

      --acknowledge-unknown-outcome
          Acknowledge that no remote success/failure is being inferred

      --json
          Emit one stable JSON object instead of human-readable text

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli audit status =====
Verify the ledger and report pending operations without changing it

Usage: serctl_cli audit status [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


Options:
      --anchor <FILE>
          Optional previously exported checkpoint used as a rollback anchor

      --anchor-output <NEW_FILE>
          Write the current authenticated checkpoint to a new file

      --json
          Emit one stable JSON object instead of human-readable text

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli down =====
Stop a running daemon after verifying one profile passphrase

Usage: serctl_cli down [NAME]

Arguments:
  [NAME]


Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli download =====
Download a remote file without overwriting an existing local file

Usage: serctl_cli download [OPTIONS] <NAME> <REMOTE> <LOCAL>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


  <REMOTE>


  <LOCAL>


Options:
      --timeout-secs <TIMEOUT_SECS>
          Hard deadline for the complete SFTP operation

          [default: 300]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli exec =====
Run a remote command through the on-demand global broker

Usage: serctl_cli exec [OPTIONS] <NAME> <CMD>...

Arguments:
  <NAME>


  <CMD>...


Options:
      --timeout-secs <TIMEOUT_SECS>
          Hard deadline for the remote command

          [default: 300]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli grant-issue =====
Issue a policy-bounded OperationGrant for an agent frontend

Usage: serctl_cli grant-issue [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


Options:
      --operations <OPERATIONS>
          Comma-separated protocol operation kinds, such as ssh.exec, sftp.list, sftp.write (create-dir only), transfer.read, transfer.write, transfer.status, transfer.cancel, forward.local/open, forward.remote/open, forward.dynamic/open, forward.status, forward.cancel, or ssh.connection-identity

      --budget <BUDGET>
          Maximum number of relayed operations (1..=1000)

          [default: 32]

      --ttl-minutes <TTL_MINUTES>
          Capability lifetime in whole minutes (1..=40; default 30)

          [default: 30]

      --profile-passphrase-handle <HANDLE_OR_FD>
          Read the profile passphrase once from an inherited HANDLE/fd

      --output <FILE>
          Create a protected file and write the grant plus private key to it

      --output-handle <HANDLE_OR_FD>
          Write to a caller-created, empty protected file HANDLE/fd, then close it

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli list =====
List saved profiles (host/port only — secrets stay sealed)

Usage: serctl_cli list

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli profile-password =====
Manage one profile's independent passphrase

Usage: serctl_cli profile-password <NAME> <COMMAND>

Commands:
  change         Change the passphrase after proving the current profile passphrase
  rotate-random  Generate and install a new random passphrase after proving the current one
  admin-reset    Administratively recover or replace a profile passphrase
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  <NAME>


Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli profile-password admin-reset =====
Administratively recover or replace a profile passphrase.

`--media` preserves sealed SSH credentials through the 2-of-2 recovery path. `--replace-credentials` discards them and requires new values; the administrator password alone can never reveal or preserve them.

Usage: serctl_cli profile-password <NAME> admin-reset [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --target-user <USER>
          Linux root: NSS account whose vault will be destructively reset. The process irreversibly drops to this account before opening it

      --host <HOST>


      --user <USER>


      --port <PORT>
          [default: 22]

      --host-key-sha256 <SHA256:FINGERPRINT>
          Expected SSH host-key fingerprint, in `SHA256:...` form

      --media <FILE>
          Offline share used to preserve and rewrap the current credentials

      --replace-credentials
          Discard the old encrypted credentials and require a full replacement

      --random
          Generate the replacement profile passphrase instead of prompting

      --random-output <FILE>
          Protected create-new file that receives the random passphrase before the vault mutation is allowed to commit

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== serctl_cli profile-password change =====
Change the passphrase after proving the current profile passphrase

Usage: serctl_cli profile-password <NAME> change

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli profile-password rotate-random =====
Generate and install a new random passphrase after proving the current one.

The new passphrase is durably written before the vault is changed, so an output failure can never strand the profile behind an unseen value.

Usage: serctl_cli profile-password <NAME> rotate-random --random-output <FILE>

Options:
      --random-output <FILE>


  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== serctl_cli recovery =====
Manage the vault-wide 2-of-2 offline recovery policy

Usage: serctl_cli recovery <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init        Initialize vault-wide offline recovery. Unix root only
  rotate      Replace the vault-wide offline share and every profile recovery envelope
  migrate-v2  Migrate a legacy v2 vault to independent profile passphrases
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli recovery init =====
Initialize vault-wide offline recovery. Unix root only

Usage: serctl_cli recovery init <NEW_MEDIA>

Arguments:
  <NEW_MEDIA>


Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli recovery migrate-v2 =====
Migrate a legacy v2 vault to independent profile passphrases

Usage: serctl_cli recovery migrate-v2 --recovery-media <FILE>

Options:
      --recovery-media <FILE>
          New 2-of-2 offline recovery share. The path must not already exist

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli recovery rotate =====
Replace the vault-wide offline share and every profile recovery envelope

Usage: serctl_cli recovery rotate --old-media <FILE> --new-media <FILE>

Options:
      --old-media <FILE>


      --new-media <FILE>


  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli transfer =====
Observable, cancellable file transfer with remote-confirmed progress

Usage: serctl_cli transfer <COMMAND>

Commands:
  push    Push a local file to a new remote destination
  pull    Pull a remote file to a new local destination
  status  Read sanitized transfer snapshots for one profile
  cancel  Cancel one active transfer owned by this profile
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli transfer cancel =====
Cancel one active transfer owned by this profile

Usage: serctl_cli transfer cancel <NAME> <TRANSFER_ID>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


  <TRANSFER_ID>


Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli transfer pull =====
Pull a remote file to a new local destination

Usage: serctl_cli transfer pull [OPTIONS] <NAME> <REMOTE> <LOCAL>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


  <REMOTE>


  <LOCAL>


Options:
      --backend <BACKEND>
          Backend selection: auto probes native then reports an explicit SFTP fallback

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, native, sftp]

      --resume <RESUME>
          Resume policy. `auto` requires the native backend and fails closed if unavailable

          [default: never]
          [possible values: auto, never]

      --idle-timeout-secs <IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS>
          Fail after this many seconds without newly confirmed remote bytes

          [default: 30]

      --deadline-secs <DEADLINE_SECS>
          Optional hard deadline for the complete transfer, independent of idle time

      --progress <PROGRESS>
          Progress output: terminal display, stable NDJSON, quiet, or TTY auto-detection

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, tty, json, quiet]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli transfer push =====
Push a local file to a new remote destination

Usage: serctl_cli transfer push [OPTIONS] <NAME> <LOCAL> <REMOTE>

Arguments:
  <NAME>


  <LOCAL>


  <REMOTE>


Options:
      --backend <BACKEND>
          Backend selection: auto probes native then reports an explicit SFTP fallback

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, native, sftp]

      --resume <RESUME>
          Resume policy. `auto` requires the native backend and fails closed if unavailable

          [default: never]
          [possible values: auto, never]

      --idle-timeout-secs <IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS>
          Fail after this many seconds without newly confirmed remote bytes

          [default: 30]

      --deadline-secs <DEADLINE_SECS>
          Optional hard deadline for the complete transfer, independent of idle time

      --progress <PROGRESS>
          Progress output: terminal display, stable NDJSON, quiet, or TTY auto-detection

          [default: auto]
          [possible values: auto, tty, json, quiet]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli transfer status =====
Read sanitized transfer snapshots for one profile

Usage: serctl_cli transfer status [OPTIONS] <NAME> [TRANSFER_ID]

Arguments:
  <NAME>


  [TRANSFER_ID]


Options:
      --watch


      --json


  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli tunnel =====
Run a loopback-only SSH TCP tunnel in the foreground until Ctrl+C

Usage: serctl_cli tunnel [OPTIONS] <NAME> <COMMAND>

Commands:
  local    Listen on local 127.0.0.1 and reach the SSH host's 127.0.0.1 port
  remote   Listen on the SSH host's 127.0.0.1 and reach this machine's loopback port
  dynamic  Dynamic SOCKS5 forwarding, listening only on local 127.0.0.1
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  <NAME>


Options:
      --profile-passphrase-handle <HANDLE_OR_FD>
          Read the profile passphrase once from an inherited HANDLE/fd

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli tunnel dynamic =====
Dynamic SOCKS5 forwarding, listening only on local 127.0.0.1

Usage: serctl_cli tunnel <NAME> dynamic [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --port <PORT>
          Loopback listener port. Use 0 to let the operating system choose one

          [default: 0]

      --max-connections <MAX_CONNECTIONS>
          Maximum number of simultaneously forwarded TCP connections

          [default: 32]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli tunnel local =====
Listen on local 127.0.0.1 and reach the SSH host's 127.0.0.1 port

Usage: serctl_cli tunnel <NAME> local [OPTIONS] --target-port <TARGET_PORT>

Options:
      --port <PORT>
          Loopback listener port. Use 0 to let the operating system choose one

          [default: 0]

      --max-connections <MAX_CONNECTIONS>
          Maximum number of simultaneously forwarded TCP connections

          [default: 32]

      --target-port <TARGET_PORT>
          Port on 127.0.0.1 of the already connected SSH host

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== serctl_cli tunnel remote =====
Listen on the SSH host's 127.0.0.1 and reach this machine's loopback port

Usage: serctl_cli tunnel <NAME> remote [OPTIONS] --target-port <TARGET_PORT>

Options:
      --port <PORT>
          Loopback listener port. Use 0 to let the operating system choose one

          [default: 0]

      --max-connections <MAX_CONNECTIONS>
          Maximum number of simultaneously forwarded TCP connections

          [default: 32]

      --target-port <TARGET_PORT>
          Port on this serctl machine's 127.0.0.1

  -h, --help
          Print help
